title: Enable NAT with iptables for internet sharing
summary: Configure iptables to perform Network Address Translation (NAT) and allow forwarding of traffic from the client interface to the internet interface.
prerequisites: Static IP is set on the client interface

steps.explain: Enable masquerading (NAT) on the internet-facing interface. This hides the client's private IP behind the server's public IP.

placeholders.name: INTERNET_INTERFACE
placeholders.description: Name of the interface connected to the internet

steps.explain: Allow forwarding of established and related connections back to the clients.
steps.cmd: sudo iptables -A FORWARD -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT

steps.explain: Allow forwarding of new connections from the client interface to the internet interface.

placeholders.name: CLIENT_INTERFACE
placeholders.description: Name of the interface connected to the client(s)

placeholders.name: INTERNET_INTERFACE
placeholders.description: Name of the interface connected to the internet

rollback.explain: To undo this, reboot the machine or manually remove the specific iptables rules using 'iptables -D' with the exact same arguments used to add them.

warnings: These rules are temporary and will be lost after a reboot.
If you use Docker, you may need to use -I DOCKER-USER instead of -A FORWARD for the forwarding rules.
Flushing iptables removes all existing rules, which might disrupt other services.
